findings.description: publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance a public endpoint and DNS name, placing a data-tier resource at the internet edge where only the security group separates it from untrusted networks.
storage_encrypted = false disables RDS storage encryption, so the database volumes and any snapshots hold catalog data in cleartext.

The master username is the predictable privileged value 'admin' and the password comes from var.password, which is persisted in plaintext Terraform state and reused in EC2 user_data instead of being managed by a secrets service; ignore_changes on password also removes any rotation path via Terraform.

findings.issue_category: no TLS enforcement for DB connections
findings.description: Neither the parameter group nor the instance enforces require_secure_transport, and the generated PHP client calls mysqli_connect without SSL, so credentials and query data can traverse the network in cleartext to a publicly reachable endpoint.

The RDS master username and var.password are interpolated into user_data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. user_data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF, and is visible in the EC2 console and Terraform state, leaking database master credentials.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available on a web server running user-supplied-input PHP; an SSRF could retrieve both the near-administrative instance profile credentials and the user_data containing the DB password.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the EBS root volume storing dbinfo.inc with database credentials may be unencrypted at rest unless account-level EBS default encryption applies.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached via instance profile to an internet-facing web server. Theft of the instance credentials yields account-wide data exfiltration from S3/RDS and privilege escalation through EC2 (e.g. launching instances with other roles).
The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and command-and-control path from the data tier.
